utterances.speaker: JUDGE MARTIN-CANIVELL
utterances.text: Good afternoon, ladies and gentlemen. Could the registrar -- do you hear me? Okay. Could the registrar please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Case number IT-95-11-PT, the Prosecutor --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MARTIN-CANIVELL
utterances.text: I don't hear.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Case number IT-95-11-PT, the Prosecutor versus --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MARTIN-CANIVELL
utterances.text: Excuse me, but I don't hear anything. I don't know what's the matter.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MARTIN-CANIVELL
utterances.text: Case number IT-95-11-PT, the Prosecutor versus Milan Martic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MARTIN-CANIVELL
utterances.text: May we have the appearances, please. For the Prosecution?

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honour. For the Prosecution today -- can you hear me? Can you hear me?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MARTIN-CANIVELL
utterances.text: Yes, now. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Okay. For the Prosecution, we have legal officer Sabine Bauer, case manager Diane Boles, and my name is Hildegard Uertz-Retzlaff.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MARTIN-CANIVELL
utterances.text: Thank you. And for the Defence?

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone for the counsel, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: Sorry. [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Your Honour. My name is Predrag Milovancevic, attorney from Belgrade. I represent Mr. Milan Martic before this Tribunal. I am joined today by our legal assistant, Mr. Vuk Sekulic, also an attorney from Belgrade.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MARTIN-CANIVELL
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Martic, can you hear the proceeding in a language that you can understand?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MARTIN-CANIVELL
utterances.text: Thank you. First of all, if you would allow me to present myself, because it's the first time I appear in this Tribunal before the parties in this case in which I have been assigned as a Judge to the Chamber and designated as a trial judge for this special case. I would like to begin by making some comments about what I know has been said in the previous two days ago in a meeting held under the 65 ter article of the Rules. And first of all, I would announce -- I would like to announce that in a few days a decision will be rendered on the motion that is still pending to be decided. Secondly, if I understand what you had then in the previous -- in this meeting previous to this Status Conference, there doesn't seem to have -- to exist problems around the Prosecutor disclosure issues. So that is to -- to be happy of this situation. And last thing, that in the future the parties could meet with sufficient interest and sufficient time for trying to find out if they can agree on some of the facts. As you may know, the counsel of the Defence, the Prosecution has pointed out a number of questions or facts that may be agreeable to you. And in this case, that could accomplish some of the ends of this Judge -- Pre-Trial Judge and at the trial time of the proceedings, because this way it will drive to a more expeditious solution of the case. On the other side, I have heard that the Prosecution has expressed the intention of trying to complete their preparatory brief, the brief prior to the trial by the month of October. So there seems to be very good news, and I hope you are keeping these expectations you have shown so far in that the Defence, the counsel for the Defence, would be able to be through all the tasks that are now ahead, to be in the possibility for this Court beginning the case around November. That is, it's possible. That would be a great solution to allow the expeditious decision of the case. On the other side, I noticed also that the number of witnesses proposed is around 60, and that should be also interesting to keep to this number if that is possible so as to have also a decision as soon as possible. Of course, if you have problems about the protection of these witnesses, you may tell the Trial Court about this, and in due time you would receive the protection perhaps you are asking for. I don't know if in this moment - this is one of the purposes of the Status Conference - some of the parties have any suggestion or any issue to be brought to my attention now. Please, if this is the case, I would thank you that you present the issues you have in mind now.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Your Honour, your observations were entirely correct, and there is actually nothing to add to this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MARTIN-CANIVELL
utterances.text: Okay. The counsel for the Defence, does it have any special issue to raise now?

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] With your permission, Your Honour, I would like to say that at this moment we don't have any problems regarding this trial. But there is an important issue which I would like to raise in connection with disclosure under Rule 68, disclosure of exculpatory documents. This week, the Prosecution has begun to disclose such documents, and we are glad to see this new development. We do believe it would be important, however, for both parties in these proceedings to be aware of that, and this is also important for the Tribunal. That's why I'm raising the issue. The Prosecution has notified us that they are going electronically through their files and documents in order to meet their obligation under Rule 69 [as interpreted]. However, they are short of personnel and there are very many documents, several thousands of such documents. The search will take some time, and they will then deliver these documents to us. Then they propose that we search through these documents and single out those which the Defence believes might be exculpatory. Another thing I wanted to raise is the Defence is prepared to help the Prosecution in this effort, but we do believe it might be worth pointing out that it would not be good or beneficial for the disclosure procedure if there were any delays or if the Defence were given too many documents to deal with and then look through. The Defence expects that the Prosecution will meet their obligation in a quick and efficient way so as to give the Defence sufficient time to prepare and start working on these documents in order to look through them in a timely manner and thus help both the Prosecution and the Court to have an expeditious trial. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MARTIN-CANIVELL
utterances.text: Thank you. I understand what you mean, and I suppose that you will have time enough before you have to appear again in the meeting prepared according to the Rule 65 ter and to have been through all the materials you would require. Otherwise, you have to -- perhaps have to ask for some more time. That should be decided in the right moment. If there is no other questions you would like to raise now, I would turn now to Mr. Martic and ask him, please, Mr. Martic, could you tell me if you have any problems related to your situation that you would like to present to me in this moment, related to your mental and physical condition, for one thing, and also to conditions -- to the conditions of your prison, actually.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much for giving me this opportunity to speak, Your Honour. With all due respect for my Defence counsel, my Defence team, I do have a series of objections, but I'd only like to raise one of them for the time being. I hope you will be patient enough to listen to my brief monologue outlining my dissatisfaction. I am speaking about the double standards applied by this Tribunal, specifically the Prosecution, the double standards applied to us Serbs but also the others. Please allow me to explain. As you are well aware, I arrived here more than a year ago, and at one time I was the president of the Republic of Serbian Krajina, whose territory was under the protection of the peacekeeping forces of the UN. The people of the area have been ethnically cleansed during the peacekeeping mission and prior to the duration of the peacekeeping mission; hundreds of crimes against my people had been carried out. Unfortunately, to this very day no Croatian leaders have been brought to justice to answer for their crimes, no perpetrators even. I am talking about the low-ranking perpetrators. As you are well aware, the Prosecution had at that time threatened the president of the Republic of Croatia, Franjo Tudjman, and the Defence Minister, Gojko Susak with indictments, and there probably would have been indictments if they were still alive. Janko Bobetko, the general, was threatened too. I suspect the same fate would await Mr. Izetbegovic. However, he just stubbornly refuses to die.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MARTIN-CANIVELL
utterances.text: [Previous interpretation continues] ... Matters could be decided at a later moment. It's not specially related to the facts we are asking -- I am asking you about. It's just your situation in the Detention Unit, if it requires some complaint or -- to inform me about your situation there, if it is acceptable, you have any problems. Other problems would be normal to mention now are if you have time and facilities adequate to speak to your counsel. And of course, if you have any troubles with your health.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Please allow me, Your Honour. This is pertinent, I believe, and I would just like to add two final sentences, if you allow. I have an obligation to my own people, people that have been ethnically cleansed. I assume it should be your obligation too, the obligation of this Tribunal. I assume this Tribunal has a preference and that's the face it shows in public as a tribunal of justice. This is the last chance to avoid presenting Croatia as an innocent party, and I believe that some of their perpetrators should be brought to justice to answer here for their crimes. I am not afraid of my own trial. Those who are righteous should not be afraid of anything. That's what my people say. That's all I wish to say, and I have nothing further to add.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MARTIN-CANIVELL
utterances.text: I would say that you tried to go outside of the scope of this meeting. Nevertheless, I conclude that what is in relation with your health and your situation in the prison doesn't deserve a special consideration from your part, and so I take for granted that you are okay and that you don't raise at this moment any question about this. Please sit down. I thank you now, the persons that represent here the Prosecution, and also to the Registry. And now I declare that this meeting arrives to a close.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the Status Conference adjourned at
